outcome.answer: The closest matches are [1], [2], [3], [4], and [6]. [1] studies on-policy distillation failures where student-generated rollouts become too long and repetitive, and proposes a stabilization method to reduce repetition-induced length inflation. [2] focuses on excessive length caused by termination-token mismatch and shows that treating equivalent EOS tokens as a shared stopping action helps curb length inflation. [4] proposes Early Stopping Rollout, which restricts generation to the first response tokens to improve training stability and efficiency. [3] and [6] also address making student-generated reasoning less verbose: [3] adds a concise-learning objective to reduce output length, while [6] mitigates weak teacher supervision over long chains, which helps prevent drift during long reasoning.
